sources.publisher: ENI SEIS II East / European Environment Agency
sources.title: C11 — Nutrients in freshwater of Georgia
supports: River and lake nitrate is reported as mg NO3-N/L.
Groundwater nitrate is reported as mg NO3/L.
Groundwater analysis covers 2016-2017; data were available for 34 of 45 sites and sampling frequency was twice per year.

sources.title: Nitrate and nitrite chemical fact sheet, Guidelines for drinking-water quality, fourth edition incorporating first and second addenda
supports: Conversion factor: 1 mg/L as nitrate ion equals 0.226 mg/L as nitrate-nitrogen. This rounded factor is for unit conversion only, not a legal limit.

sources.title: Government Decree №58/2014 — Drinking Water Technical Regulation
supports: Nitrate limit 50 mg/L as NO3- and nitrite limit 0.2 mg/L as NO2- for water within the decree's scope.

sources.title: Government Decree №58/2014 — surface-water national maximum permissible concentrations as reported by EEA C11
supports: The EEA C11 page reports separate surface-water nitrate values of 45 mg NO3/L (10.2 mg NO3-N/L) for cyprinid waters and 40 mg NO3/L (9.0 mg NO3-N/L) for salmonid waters; these are not drinking-water limits.

conversion.precision_note: The published factor is rounded; converted values must retain source basis and must not be treated as more precise than the original measurement.

comparability_guards: Do not pool river/lake and groundwater values without an explicit basis conversion and preservation of the original source value.
Do not compare surface-water ecological thresholds with drinking-water health limits.
Do not treat raw groundwater as drinking water without confirming intended use, sampling point and legal scope.
Do not use converted rounded values for a legal pass/fail decision near a threshold; use the applicable source's native unit and legal text.
Do not infer current 2026 exposure from the 2016-2017 groundwater aggregate.
